page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2.7xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with hyperthreading on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. It includes 128 GB of RAM, providing 4 GB of memory per vCPU, alongside 33 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 vector instruction support. The instance runs under KVM hypervision and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps. It does not bundle local NVMe SSD storage or discrete GPU devices, relying entirely on network-attached volume storage.

Synthetic benchmarks highlight a trade-off between single-thread latency and multi-threaded scaling. Single-core performance falls in the lower percentile, reflected by a stress-ng single-core result of 1108.99 and a Geekbench single-core score of 967.0. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput achieves average tier results, marked by a PassMark CPU score of 23056.78 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 23516.07. Application tests show steady throughput, yielding 23.19 million Redis SET operations per second and 13.88 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks.

From a resource-density perspective, this server delivers standard memory and vCPU proportions suited for parallel computing without requiring high clock rates. The main limitations reside in weaker single-threaded speed and the necessity of external persistent storage. Workloads best aligned with this hardware profile include multi-threaded backend applications, distributed web server pools, software build systems, and medium-scale database deployments using block storage.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2.7xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on x86_64 architecture, powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor with 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores and 128 GB of RAM. Operating on a KVM hypervisor, it features 33 MB of L3 cache, AVX-512 instruction support, and a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps. The server carries no local disk storage or GPU hardware. In benchmark testing, the instance exhibits below-average single-core CPU performance but reaches middle-tier capacity in multi-core metrics, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 23056.78 and 23.19 million Redis SET operations per second. The balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it qualitatively cost-effective for multi-threaded server workloads, software compilation, medium-scale database operations, and web serving, provided workloads do not require high per-thread performance or local NVMe storage.
